name: Technocracy
summary: Technocracy holds that government should be run by experts using scientific, evidence-based and efficiency-minded methods rather than by partisan politics. Legitimacy comes from competence and results rather than from elections or ideology. It pursues a single long-term common good, worked out by reason, instead of bargaining between competing interests. In practice it usually appears as a hybrid, with key functions such as monetary policy and regulation handed to independent expert bodies.
scope: The mainstream doctrine of rule by expertise as it exists today, in hybrid technocratic governance (independent central banks, EU expert institutions, Singapore-style meritocratic administration, technocratic cabinets), as described in Wikipedia's overview and in Caramani's and Bertsou and Caramani's political-science work. Its intellectual lineage runs from Saint-Simon through Veblen's 'soviet of technicians'. It excludes the specific economic program of the 1930s Technocracy Inc. movement (energy certificates replacing money, a continental technate), which is used only as a historical reference point.

furtherReading.title: Technocracy (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: A broad overview of the idea, its history, modern examples and critiques.

furtherReading.title: Technocracy movement (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: The 1930s North American movement that popularised the word.

furtherReading.title: The Engineers and the Price System (Thorstein Veblen, 1921)
furtherReading.note: The classic case for handing industry to engineers, ending with the 'soviet of technicians'.

furtherReading.title: Letters from an Inhabitant of Geneva (Saint-Simon, 1803)
furtherReading.note: An early text by the 'father of technocracy' arguing that scientists should lead society.

keyFigures.name: Henri de Saint-Simon
keyFigures.role: Early proponent of rule by scientists and industrial experts

keyFigures.name: Thorstein Veblen
keyFigures.role: Proposed a "soviet of technicians" in The Engineers and the Price System

sources.author: Eri Bertsou and Daniele Caramani, AJPS blog summary
sources.usedFor: Technocratic attitudes: preference for expertise, anti-politics, dissatisfaction with representative democracy, non-extreme left-right placement

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from technocrats' deference to public-health expertise and the comprehensive public services of Keynesian-style technocratic states, though neoliberal technocrats prefer market mechanisms.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Technocracy has no commitment either way; it would set wages by economic evidence, and expert opinion on large increases is genuinely divided.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The family is split: Veblen and the 1930s movement rejected the price system outright, while today's neoliberal technocracy manages markets through competition and risk regulation.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership is treated as secondary to competent management; Keynesian technocrats favoured state enterprise and neoliberal ones privatisation, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are seen as a technical question for cost-benefit analysis rather than a principle, and technocratic governments have both raised and cut them.

unions-good.rationale: Technocracy rejects brokering between organised interests in favour of one expert-defined common good, and Veblen dismissed trade unions as rival groups fixed on 'the full dinner-pail'.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is subordinate to efficiency and the common good; Veblen proposed voiding absentee ownership, though modern technocrats rarely go that far.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Technocrats want expert regulators to discipline business, from Veblen's charge that business sabotages output to modern delegation of regulation to expert agencies.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare spending would be judged by measured outcomes, not by principle, and technocratic regimes range from generous Keynesian states to lean ones like Singapore.

worker-ownership.rationale: Technocracy gives control to technically trained managers, not to the workforce as a whole; even Veblen's council was of engineers rather than workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's risk-management and cost-benefit reasoning, which tends to accept security measures that experts judge effective; critics note its risk of techno-authoritarianism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy would follow evidence on harms, and technocrats differ on what that evidence recommends; the ideology takes no stand of its own.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech regulation is not a technocratic concern, and nothing in its texts settles it; inferred indifference.

strong-leader.rationale: Scholars contrast technocracy, which entrusts authority to experts reasoning about the public good, with populism, which entrusts it to a leader who embodies the people's will; technocracy is also distinguished from authoritarianism.

state-harmful.rationale: Technocracy is a doctrine of expert administration that extends the state's capacity to plan and regulate, the opposite of anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from deference to public-health evidence on firearm harms; technocratic texts do not address guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Technocracy has no stated position on security spending; it would allocate it by assessed need.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in technocratic thought; would be settled by evidence on harms, on which adherents differ.

decide-locally.rationale: Technocracy favours centralised, uniform expert solutions such as national directorates or continental planning, and critics fault it precisely for ignoring local context.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from evidence-based policy: technocrats would favour whatever lowers reoffending, which research generally ties to rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Family structure lies outside technocracy's concerns, and its texts do not address it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by technocratic thought, which has no moral doctrine on marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Technocracy offers no moral position on abortion, and its claim to value-neutrality leaves such questions to others.

more-religion-public.rationale: Technocratic thought puts scientific knowledge in place of theology and metaphysics; Saint-Simon wanted scientists to hold the 'spiritual power'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not part of technocratic doctrine; would be judged by measured outcomes.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Technocracy takes no position on theories of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from its orientation to progress: Saint-Simon set the progressive 'progress of the human mind' against the proprietors' 'No innovation!'.

gradual-change.rationale: Modern technocracy works through established institutions such as central banks and expert agencies and values stability, though Veblen and the 1930s movement sought a sweeping overturn.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Technocracy has no stated view on immigration levels, and technocratic governments have managed migration very differently.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Expert-led supranational bodies such as the EU's institutions and the European Central Bank are standard examples of technocratic governance.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from deference to mainstream economic expertise; the 1930s movement's self-sufficient continental technate is an exception.

nation-first.rationale: Technocracy aims at a long-term common good worked out by reason, not national self-interest; Saint-Simon described wars as clashes of private interests.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed by technocratic thought; it has no doctrine on borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Technocracy aims at productive efficiency and abundance; Veblen attacked business for restricting output, though modern technocrats also apply ecological evidence.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Technocratic governance applies scientific evidence to climate and environmental regulation, and adherents defer to climate science.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technocrats trust science and engineering to deliver prosperity; the 1930s movement held that technology had made abundance possible.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from deference to engineering expertise and the movement's focus on energy; no technocratic text cited here addresses nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Technocrats opposed communist revolution and modern technocracy works through institutions, though Veblen envisaged an 'overturn' by a general strike of technicians.

experts-over-public.rationale: This is the core of technocracy: legitimacy comes from expertise rather than from popular will.

central-planning.rationale: Adherents split: Veblen and the 1930s movement wanted engineers to plan the whole economy, while most present-day technocrats run central banks and regulators within a market economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Technocracy cares about who manages, not about worker or public ownership, so it would not make markets conditional on ownership.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; it would be treated as a technical fiscal question.

basic-income.rationale: Not part of the mainstream doctrine; the 1930s movement's equal energy certificates resemble one, but modern technocrats are divided.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from deference to mainstream economic expertise, which generally opposes protection; the 1930s technate's self-sufficiency points the other way.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Technocratic developmental states such as Singapore and post-1978 China, like Veblen's directorate allocating resources among industries, have experts steer investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Technocracy values efficiency at scale; Veblen praised chain stores and mail-order houses over wasteful small competitors.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Technocracy Inc. wanted money replaced by energy certificates, but mainstream technocracy entrusts the management of money to experts rather than abolishing it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Independent central banks run by unelected experts are a model technocratic institution.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Technocracy seeks one rational common good rather than negotiated settlements between organised groups.

one-party-rule.rationale: Technocracy claims to stand above partisanship and ideology and is analysed as a challenge to party government, though China combines technocrats with one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy comes from competence, not birth, and Saint-Simon wanted power to follow enlightenment.

democracy-best.rationale: Technocracy grounds legitimacy in expertise and long-term responsibility rather than votes, and people with technocratic attitudes are dissatisfied with representative democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Putting laws to popular vote is the opposite of entrusting policy to experts, which scholars set against populism's appeal to the people's will.

workers-councils.rationale: Technocracy wants councils of technical experts, not of workers; Veblen's 'soviet' was of technicians and excluded the rank and file.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from its preference for large, integrated planning units such as continental technates and supranational bodies.

natural-rulers.rationale: Technocracy is a form of elitism and meritocracy: those with superior competence should govern, from Plato's philosopher-kings to Saint-Simon's scientists.

political-violence-never.rationale: Technocrats generally reject revolutionary violence and prefer orderly administration; Veblen hoped owners would abdicate without force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from its idea of a rational common good; Saint-Simon saw wars as clashes of private interests.

separate-church-state.rationale: Technocracy is secular and scientistic, grounding policy in evidence rather than religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Technocracy derives policy from scientific method and evidence, which rules out scripture as a basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: technocracy enlarges public expert administration rather than privatising core state functions.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy rests on competence and a rational common good, not ethnicity; the movement called itself anti-fascist.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Technocrats opposed communist revolution and see history in terms of science and technical progress rather than class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed by mainstream technocracy; the 1930s movement's equal energy allotments are an exception, and modern technocrats differ.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: technocracy organises around functional and technical units, not religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Technocracy puts a long-term common good above private interest, and Veblen condemned profit-seeking for sabotaging production.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from its anti-pluralist focus on a single common good, which ranks the collective interest above individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from its instrumental rationality and cost-benefit methods, which value nature for its use to people.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Technocracy is the governing doctrine of industrial modernity and sees industry, managed rationally, as the source of abundance.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from its faith in technical progress; modern technocracy also values institutional stability, which tempers this.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from its trust in science and technology; not addressed in technocratic texts.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic governance ('algocracy') is discussed as an extension of technocratic, data-driven decision-making, though most adherents keep humans in charge.

restore-past-order.rationale: Technocracy is oriented to progress; Saint-Simon cast innovation and the 'progress of the human mind' against those who resist it.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Judging policy by measured results and evidence rather than ideology is technocracy's defining claim.

direct-action.rationale: Technocracy works through institutions and expert bodies, and the 1930s movement shunned both elections and agitation; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's instrumental rationality and its judging of policy by results.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Technocracy sees rationally managed industry as the source of abundance.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rule by specialists rests on the division of labor and expertise.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mainstream technocracy accepts distribution through wages and markets; the 1930s movement's equal energy certificates are an exception.

production-for-use.rationale: Adherents split: Veblen and the 1930s movement attacked production for profit, while today's technocrats manage market economies.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Veblen charged absentee owners with sabotaging production, not with exploiting labor, and modern technocrats accept profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Technocrats opposed communist revolution and want rule by experts, not by a class.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from deference to mainstream economics and from Saint-Simon's view of industrial society as peaceful.

taxation-theft.rationale: Technocracy extends the state's capacity to plan and regulate and treats taxation as a technical tool.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from technocrats' willingness to regulate self-regarding risks when evidence shows harm, as in public-health policy.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy distrusts electoral voice but has no theory of exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Adherents split: neoliberal technocrats apply business management to the state, while Veblen and the 1930s movement rejected the price system.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from deference to mainstream scientific consensus, which attributes group differences mainly to environment.

organic-representation.rationale: Technocracy wants representation by experts reasoning about the common good, not by organized groups.

total-state.rationale: Technocracy extends expert management over the economy and regulation but does not claim to direct culture or all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred from its orientation to progress rather than nationalist renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from its rational common-good outlook; the 1930s continental technate is an exception.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on competence and impersonal expertise, the opposite of personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from its meritocratic, efficiency-minded outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: Technocracy claims value-neutrality and takes no moral doctrine.

single-common-good.rationale: Anti-pluralism, the pursuit of one rationally identified general interest instead of mediating between groups, is a defining feature of technocracy.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred from its efficiency-minded preference for practical solutions over symbolic national projects.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Technocracy gives authority to experts rather than to votes, and treats broad participation in running institutions as less reliable than competence.

school-vouchers.rationale: Treated as an empirical question for evidence on outcomes; neoliberal technocrats favor choice mechanisms while Keynesian-style ones favor public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The family is split between Keynesian technocrats who accept stimulus and neoliberal or central-bank technocrats who favor fiscal rules; the stance is judged by expert analysis.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: technocrats prize expert-run efficiency over liberty as such, and the tradition spans Veblen's centrally planned economy and neoliberal expert regimes, so adherents split on whether freedom needs free markets.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from technocracy's reliance on expert-designed rules, institutions and measurable results rather than the personal virtue of leaders.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from legitimacy resting on competence rather than nationhood, and from technocrats' comfort with supranational expert bodies such as the EU and ECB.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's preference for rule-bound, expert-run institutions, which suggests deference to the UN system over unilateral military judgment; the sources do not address it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Technocracy grounds government in scientific, evidence-based expertise and a single common good worked out by reason rather than by passion or partisan will, though 'only' overstates how it treats values and democratic input.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Technocracy has no doctrine on who qualifies for benefits; experts would judge eligibility by measured outcomes, and technocratic states differ widely on it.

positive-liberty.rationale: Technocracy is about who governs, not a theory of freedom; adherents range from Keynesian to neoliberal.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare design is left to expert judgment and technocrats of different kinds differ on conditionality.

class-collaboration.rationale: Technocracy pursues a single common good and treats partisan and class bargaining as inefficient; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Technocrats value progress and efficiency but are not defined by hostility to heritage, and the radical Technocracy Inc. agenda is excluded; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Technocracy is not defined by geopolitics, and its main forms (central banks, EU bodies) are embedded in Western institutions; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Technocracy favors expert administration over class organization of any kind; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rule by competence and merit runs against assigning public roles by sex; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Independent central banks and expert economic management take credit and interest for granted; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legitimacy from competence is at odds with ascriptive racial classification; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Technocracy claims the state can be neutral and run by experts, though Veblen saw business interests steering industry; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from technocratic deference to climate science and environmental expertise, which favors phasing out fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Technocracy is indifferent to cultural questions; it would decide integration by evidence, and technocrats are split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Technocrats rest on evidence and expert analysis, and a conspiracy theory of elite replacement conflicts with that.

proportional-representation.rationale: Technocracy has no commitment on electoral systems; it would choose the design experts consider efficient, and experts are split.

national-mission.rationale: Technocracy holds that policy follows reason and evidence, not a national calling.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Technocracy is silent on this; its experts would follow the evidence, and views among them vary.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Technocrats say that the political class is partisan, but they argue it is incompetent and short-term rather than corrupt, and trust experts instead.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Early technocrats' eugenics ties are mixed in the sources; modern technocracy has no stated position, so this is inferred from its scientific outlook.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Technocracy does not address this; expert bodies would favor accountability in general, but it is not part of the doctrine.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Technocracy gives the state broad managerial functions, from regulation to planning, and rejects a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rule by evidence-based expertise has no place for racial discouragement, which lacks scientific support; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, evidence-based approach to the common good; not a defining position.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Technocracy Inc. opposed communist revolution and partisan politics; inferred disagreement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by technocracy; adherents would not agree on this.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform rules applied by expert administration are inferred to be preferred over group-specific law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from a secular, evidence-based outlook; not addressed directly.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from evidence-based policy over religious norms; not addressed directly.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's secular, science-led approach to public institutions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Veblen's soviet of technicians and the Technocracy movement addressed no wider geopolitics of socialist states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy comes from competence and results rather than elections or consent, and technocracy is anti-pluralist.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Technocracy rests on the claim that expertise is a neutral, evidence-based guide to government, so adherents reject the idea that knowledge simply reflects power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from reliance on mainstream economic expertise, which treats the trade balance as an outcome rather than a goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the modern hybrid technocracy of liberal-democratic institutions, where expert administration works by rules and evidence rather than expulsion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Technocratic legitimacy rests on results and efficiency, so adherents judge force by outcomes rather than by an absolute rule; inferred, not stated.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Technocrats pursue a single common good worked out by reason and planned cooperation (Saint-Simon, Veblen) rather than rivalry; neoliberal variants favour competition, so this is inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anti-partisan and order-minded, technocrats would accept removing parties that threaten the expert-run order; inferred, as the issue is not stated.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom is not a central concern of technocracy, and unaccountable expert power sits uneasily with non-domination while efficiency-first rule does not address it; inferred and split.

separated-powers.rationale: Independent expert bodies divide power from elected politicians, but technocrats distrust partisan checks and bargaining; adherents are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Technocrats want rule by experts, not by a revolutionary party, and the 1930s Technocracy movement explicitly opposed communist revolution and partisan politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Technocracy has no commitment either way; it would set priorities by evidence of need and efficiency, and experts differ on prioritising the poorest.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Technocracy has no stake in housing tenure; it would decide on evidence, and experts are divided on the effects of selling off social housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Technocrats would regulate industrial action on evidence of economic cost, but the doctrine does not commit to restricting or protecting strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Technocrats defer to demographic and economic research, which does not support population growth as the main cause of poverty, but the doctrine itself takes no stand.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Technocracy claims value-neutral, evidence-based rule, and social-science evidence on diversity and cohesion is mixed; inferred from that stance, it would not accept the claim as stated.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Technocracy rests legitimacy on competence, and Wikipedia and Caramani describe it as set against selection by popular will; random selection of laypeople contradicts rule by experts. Inferred from that principle.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Independent expert bodies and the rule of law are part of hybrid technocratic governance, so suspending legal protections is disfavoured, though technocrats accept emergency powers exercised by experts. Inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economists and technocrats in the neoliberal and Keynesian variants generally distrust price ceilings as causing shortages, though emergency controls have been used. Inferred from the evidence-based stance.

party-controls-media.rationale: Technocracy prizes claimed neutrality and independent expert institutions, not party-run information; but Singapore and China-style variants do control media, so adherents differ. Inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Technocracy places power in expert state institutions rather than parties and opposes partisan politics, so party command of the army conflicts with it. Inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship timing is a matter technocrats would set by integration evidence; the doctrine takes no position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Technocrats value competent officials and pay arrangements that attract expertise, which cuts against a wage cap; the sources do not address pay directly.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Technocracy is critical of party government and partisan bargaining, but it also dislikes members voting by self-interest; inferred from its anti-partisan stance.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Technocratic governance is often hybrid and supranational, notably EU expert institutions and independent bodies handling cross-border problems.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Technocracy gives power to expert bodies, not to a head of state; Caramani contrasts it with populist leader rule.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the ideology and the sources do not address it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Legitimacy comes from scientific competence, so religious scholars holding final authority contradicts the core claim.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Saint-Simon viewed war as a clash of private interests, but technocrats are not class-war internationalists; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Technocrats are not concerned with moral censorship and favor open scientific inquiry; inferred from the Saint-Simon emphasis on progress.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not a technocratic question; expert bodies tend to value continuity but not personal executive tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Technocrats prefer judgments by competence and results over popular removal of officials; inferred from their distrust of electoral pressure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the preference for stable, expert-managed institutions and cooperative international bodies such as the EU and central banks.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on efficient, evidence-based policy; housing economists generally favor functioning rental markets, and nothing in the ideology backs forced ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from the central place of professional expertise and administration; an armed citizenry in place of professional forces runs against rule by trained specialists.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from the modernist, science-minded outlook of Saint-Simon and Veblen, which treats industry and cities as the sites of progress rather than moralizing rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Technocracy is a method of governing and has no stance on national reunification; it depends on the expert assessment of costs and benefits.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The ideology rests on trust in expertise and educated competence, so the claim that the educated are out of touch is the populist position it opposes.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The ideology does not address comparative culture; scientific universalism suggests some ranking by measurable results while its pluralism-averse stance does not settle it.

death-penalty.rationale: Technocrats defer to evidence on the effects of punishment, which varies by case; the ideology does not settle the question.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Technocrats defer to scientific and public-health expertise, which supports evidence-based sex education in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Technocracy gives authority to scientific expertise, which rejects creationism as unscientific, and Saint-Simon put scientists as the spiritual power.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not a technocratic concern; the position would turn on expert assessment of harms and adherents are split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, meritocratic bent: citizenship by descent is an ascriptive rule an administrator would see as less rational than residence.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is a matter for expert administration case by case and the ideology has no settled position.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from the stress on a single common good and uniform expert-set rules, which cut against group-specific exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy is concerned with administration, not with social conformity, and adherents are split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: technocrats prize creditworthiness and expert-managed relief, not blanket cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: technocracy centres administrative competence rather than the ownership structure of the economy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the preference for expert-designed institutions over popular drafting, which it distrusts as partisan.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from Singapore-style meritocratic administration, where results legitimise limits on political competition.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from evidence-based, efficiency-minded problem solving, which treats global poverty as a solvable technical problem.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Technocracy has no stated view; it would defer to strategic experts and adherents differ.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from distrust of popular personality contests; legitimacy comes from competence rather than elections.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Independent central banks are the standard example of hybrid technocratic governance, handing monetary policy to experts.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: technocrats favour negotiated, evidence-weighed settlements over claims of historic right.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the single common good worked out by reason, which licenses expert regulation of property use.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Veblen's soviet of technicians drew on Russia but technocrats have no settled view of the USSR's class character.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the evidence-based approach to environment in the overview, which favours acting on expert risk assessment, though experts also demand scientific proof.

collective-defense.rationale: Technocracy is about who governs, not alliances, and technocratic bodies and states have taken varied views.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; technocrats judge by results and law rather than principle, so adherents have no common stance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from Saint-Simon's scientists as the new spiritual power and a secular order of reason, which subordinates religious authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the claim of a single non-partisan common good, which fits a head of state above party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats judge by efficiency and stability rather than a shared doctrine of territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the pragmatic use of hybrid arrangements such as Singapore and China, but nothing in the sources states it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Legitimacy rests on competence and results, so sacred or hereditary claims to rule are rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Experts divide on tax design; technocratic efficiency can favour flat simplicity or progressive rates and the sources do not say.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the engineering faith in social design and abundance, which treats people as shaped by circumstances; not stated directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from rule by expert rules and mandates, which treats rulers as bound by procedure; sources do not discuss it.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the 1930s movement's emphasis on technological abundance and energy, which suits large-scale expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Technocracy is described as unitary, non-pluralist rule by experts, which rejects balancing the few against the many.

leader-cult.rationale: Caramani contrasts technocratic with populist leader-centred representation; the stress on competence over charisma rejects leader glorification.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the sources are silent and technocrats defer to child-welfare research rather than hold a doctrine.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Technocracy movement opposed communist revolution and partisan class politics, treating them as obstacles to expert management.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; experts would judge land reform by evidence of its effects, so there is no fixed position.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; expert administrators would treat it as a case-by-case policy question.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the rational, cosmopolitan outlook of rule by expertise, which has no place for ethnic claims on territory.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the secular, evidence-based and liberty-protecting character of technocratic governance.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the secular, evidence-based character of technocracy, which would not set religious dress law.

common-currency.rationale: Technocratic institutions such as independent central banks and the EU's expert bodies are the model cases; the euro is a technocratic project.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the preference for functional, expertise-based administration over identity-based politics.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats favor expert administration and uniform standards, but the question is outside their frame.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is indifferent to the identity politics behind this choice.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Veblen and the Technocracy movement held that technology and industrial organization, more than ideas or politics, shape society and make the price system obsolete.

ban-cartels.rationale: Veblen attacked business combines for sabotage and waste, so technocrats favor curbing concentrated economic power, though they would do so by expert regulation.

no-bailouts.rationale: Expert crisis management, such as central banks acting as lender of last resort, generally accepts rescues to protect the system.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Technocracy puts expert bodies such as central banks and regulators out of reach of majorities and elected politicians, and critics call this its anti-democratic side.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the competence and merit standard of legitimacy, which would oppose quotas, though technocrats might back parity if evidence supported it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The 1930s technate was a continental bloc, but mainstream technocracy rests on global expert institutions and open exchange.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the weight technocrats give to scientific evidence on environmental limits and the role of international expert bodies.

moral-incentives.rationale: Technocracy movement proposals rested on energy certificates and abundance, not moral appeals, and expert management assumes designed institutional incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Technocracy movement rejected revolution and the mainstream stands for expert administration within existing institutions; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Expertise-based legitimacy is meritocratic, so rank by birth has no standing.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Technocracy has no curriculum doctrine beyond favouring evidence-based, expert-designed education; adherents would not agree on a national-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: technocrats stress merit and competence, and Saint-Simonian progress thinking was paternalist, but modern technocracy rests on legitimacy through results, not imperial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's anti-ideological, evidence-first stance: schooling should build competence, not required civic pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats defer to empirical evidence on outcomes and would split between meritocratic and equity-driven policy design.

public-money-creation.rationale: Technocracy's hallmark is money handed to expert bodies such as independent central banks, and Veblen and Technocracy Inc. wanted money allocation run centrally by technicians rather than by private business.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Technocrats see expert management, Keynesian or neoliberal, as able to steer market economies through crises; Technocracy Inc. predicted collapse, but the mainstream hybrid strand does not.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; technocratic governance is mostly indifferent to imperial legacy and judges foreign policy by expert assessment of interests.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: technocratic institutions (EU bodies, central banks, Singapore) are built on integration and expert-managed trade; Technocracy Inc.'s continental technate is the only autarkic exception.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: this is a Marxist claim; technocrats see productivity and technology, not extraction from poor countries, as the source of rich-world wages.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: technocracy favours regulation by expert bodies and a single common good over unrestricted private choice, and has no doctrine of freedom of association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Technocrats value expert-run bodies insulated from majorities, which resembles entrenchment, but they treat rights as policy outputs rather than constitutional limits; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is indifferent to this question.

elective-rulers.rationale: Technocracy rejects hereditary rule but derives legitimacy from competence rather than elections; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Technocracy is unitary and non-pluralist, so a dissenter veto contradicts its single expert-determined common good.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rule bound by reason and law is inferred; Saint-Simon's legitimacy follows enlightenment, not a ruler's will.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Technocracy delegates key functions to independent expert bodies and is anti-pluralist rather than parliament-centered.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Scientific consensus on animal sentience is inferred to be accepted.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Evidence-based minimization of harm is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not addressed; efficiency-minded programmes rather than charity duty, split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Technocratic citizens favor leaving governing to experts, but the movement itself runs public administration; split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; the pacification thesis is inferred to be rejected by an expertise-led ideology.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; claimed neutrality of expert rule is inferred to oppose class-consent accounts.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; inferred to favor expert development policy within an open system.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices should go by competence, which the ideology states as its legitimacy principle.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; inferred to favor expert-led development using external knowledge and capital.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Competence-based office is inferred to reject ancestry-based leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Technocracy Inc. opposed both fascism and communist revolution; inferred more broadly.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Technocracy Inc. opposed both fascism and communism, which supports condemning both; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Deference to expert historical consensus is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Evidence-based policy attention to measured disadvantage is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Technocracy claims universal scientific methods, though China and Singapore variants exist; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Rule by experts rather than the army is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a technocratic concern; the doctrine is about how government is run, and committed adherents have no common view on family obligation.

office-by-exam.rationale: Technocracy puts rule by demonstrated competence at its core, and Singapore-style meritocratic administration selects officials by tested ability rather than election or patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Technocrats would decide on expert evidence of strategic risk and economic benefit; neoliberal technocrats favour open investment and others favour screening, so adherents split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from technocratic reliance on empirical evidence and a non-moralising approach to social policy, which tends to accept no-fault rules.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Technocracy rejects binding mandates because representatives should act on reason and expertise rather than the will of the electorate, which Caramani contrasts with populism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; neoliberal technocrats favour funded private accounts while Keynesian ones favour public schemes, and pension design is treated as an expert question.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from technocratic pragmatism and the efficiency case for secure, tradeable property rights; Veblen's critique targeted absentee ownership of industry, not land tenure as such.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Technocrats accept elected oversight in hybrid systems but favour expert-run fiscal rules and independent bodies, and the scholarship shows them distrusting party-driven budgeting.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred efficiency arguments for a common administrative language compete with expert-led accommodation, as with the multilingual EU institutions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from technocratic preference for evidence-based, open economic policy over blanket bans, though strategic exceptions are accepted.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; expert statistical measurement of outcomes appeals to technocrats, but they also stress intent and cost-benefit analysis, so adherents split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not a defining issue; Technocracy Inc. sought abundance, while environmental technocrats favour reducing consumption, so adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the technocratic preference for rational, institutional and multilateral management of conflict over covert proxy wars; Saint-Simon saw war as a clash of private interests.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the preference for rule-bound institutions and negotiated settlement over force; Saint-Simon's vision was of peace built by experts across states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Veblen's engineers are set against business control of industry and policy, and technocrats generally want decisions insulated from lobbying and partisan interests.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the preference for open, expert cooperation across borders; not addressed directly.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by technocracy; a technocrat could favour it on demographic evidence or oppose it as costly.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the preference for uniform, efficiency-minded rules administered by experts over local gatekeeping.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on efficiency and expert design; technocrats usually prefer targeted, evidence-based policy to open-ended guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy places expertise above democratic legitimacy, so adherents have no settled view.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on orderly, rule-based administration by experts.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the preference for expert international institutions, which a strict non-intervention rule would limit.

industrial-unions.rationale: Veblen's soviet of technicians is organised by industrial branch, which points to industry-wide organisation; inferred for unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The reason-and-evidence orientation rejects conspiracy theories; inferred, as the doctrine did not address them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by technocracy; no settled view.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the evidence-based, transparent-administration ideal; not a central doctrine.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on efficiency and specialised, large-scale expert planning.

informal-organisation.rationale: Technocracy favours expert institutions over informal groups of the like-minded and over mass politics.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Technocratic governance relies on international expert bodies such as EU institutions, so adherents tend not to put national law above them; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Technocracy is secular and expertise-based; it has no place for a religious definition of the nation, inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine concerns who governs, not relations between states, so it has no settled view; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Technocrats would set fiscal distribution by expert evidence, and experts differ; no settled view.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mainstream technocratic governance is indifferent to ownership, though Veblen and Technocracy Inc. wanted engineers managing industry; adherents split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Technocracy is a method of rule and is compatible with both capitalist and communist-ruled states, such as China; no settled view.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Technocrats judge institutions by efficiency and results, which allows mixed provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Technocracy rests on scientific rationality, and Saint-Simon put scientists as the spiritual power; inferred that religion would be seen as superseded.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Technocrats are split, with Veblen critical of business and Saint-Simon admiring industry; no settled view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not a technocratic concern; experts would decide on evidence and no commitment is stated.

socialized-care.rationale: Expert-run public services fit some technocratic states but the doctrine takes no position; split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not evidence-based policy; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Rule-bound, expert-administered legal order favors stable commitments; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Technocracy favors centralized expert management over small self-governing communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic settlement engineering is not an expert, evidence-based aim; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Technocracy claims to be beyond left and right, and Technocracy Inc. opposed both the price system and communist revolution; inferred from that.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Technocrats judge by evidence and present-day efficiency, not historical entitlement; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Technocracy rests on respect for expert and evidentiary knowledge, which denial contradicts; the sources do not discuss it directly.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the evidence-based outlook of expert governance, which finds no harm to justify penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Technocracy is anti-pluralist and some variants (Singapore, China) restrict opposition, but typical adherents defend expert rule within democratic hybrids.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Secular, evidence-based government gives no role to punishing blasphemy; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aim of a general good rather than one group's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Outside technocracy; inferred disagreement from its secular, state-centered view.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Legitimacy comes from competence and results, not religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Technocracy puts decisions in the hands of experts and treats popular bargaining as inferior, though hybrid forms keep elected bodies.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from technocracy's unitary, non-identity-based approach to the common good.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats would follow expert evidence, which adherents read differently.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; expert opinion is divided and technocracy takes no stance.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Technocracy claims to stand above partisan ideology and to draw on whatever evidence shows works.

alienated-labor.rationale: Technocrats pursue efficiency and are not much concerned with alienation; Veblen's critique targets business sabotage, not wage work as such.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from evidence-based, non-identity politics.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Legitimacy comes from competence and results, not God or the people; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between secular neutrality and tolerance.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a regulatory approach that fixes rules by evidence about harms.

social-market-economy.rationale: Technocratic states generally pair regulated markets with public services; inferred, since neoliberal and Keynesian variants differ.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Technocratic governance assumes a functioning state with security capacity; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Neoliberal technocrats accept uneven growth, Keynesian ones do not; adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; technocratic states differ (EU member, Singapore non-aligned).

dynastic-succession.rationale: Technocracy bases office on competence and merit, so inherited rule is contrary to its core claim.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a technocratic theme; expert bodies typically accept regulated profit-making banks. Inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Technocrats defer to expert financial institutions, which usually favour lender conditions on sound policy. Inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Legitimacy rests on competence, not wealth, though some technocrats favour epistocracy; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by technocracy; inferred as a split between ecological-expert views and indifference.

reification.rationale: Technocrats see social coordination as a technical matter, not as ideological distortion; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Technocracy is not centrally concerned with media ownership; its ideal has experts, not owners, steering. Inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Expert administration prefers stable, rule-based procedures, though expert discretion is also valued; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Technocracy selects by competence, so racial or ethnic limits contradict it.

online-participation.rationale: Adherents split between data-driven participation tools and distrust of popular decision-making; the sources describe algocracy but no settled view.

open-government-data.rationale: Evidence-based government implies open records and traceability; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religion-based marriage rules conflict with merit-based, secular governance; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting by religion is irrational and non-evidence-based from a technocratic view; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Technocracy grounds legitimacy in expertise and competence rather than in lay deliberation, so typical adherents prefer experts and expert bodies to citizens chosen by lot; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Technocrats prize reason and evidence over inherited authority, so they would favor adapting doctrine to modern conditions; inferred, as religion is not a core issue.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy is about who governs, and experts could favor or ignore wealth limits.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from its evidence-based, competence-first approach, which judges people by fitness rather than orientation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: it is secular and rational but about expertise in government, not promoting unbelief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that evidence-based reform of policing is favored over abolition, with expert administration retained.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its anti-pluralism: a single common good found by reason rather than shares for communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: it favors expert-run public programs over reliance on charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy comes from competence, so rotating experts out by term limit is not part of it.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegating decisions to trusted experts fits technocracy, but a revocable popular delegation system is not part of it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its evidence-based, long-term focus, which favors expert-led attention to catastrophic risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Outside the ideology; no stated position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Outside the ideology; no stated position.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Local voting rights are not a question of expertise; inferred as indifferent from technocracy's focus on competence rather than franchise.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from technocrats' deference to economic expertise, which broadly holds that price caps reduce housing supply.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from expert-led economic management, where mainstream economists see IP as a justified incentive; not a stated technocratic position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: mass drilled movements are a mobilising, ideological project, at odds with technocracy's depoliticised, evidence-based governance.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Defence posture is a policy matter technocracy leaves to experts; no stated position, so inferred as neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing is left to strategic expertise rather than principle; no stated position, so inferred as neutral.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's reliance on expert and historical evidence; formal recognition follows scholarly consensus.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Veblen's lineage, which contrasts productive engineers with absentee owners who live off ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's pragmatic, results-based ethics, which has no pacifist commitment.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's evidence-first stance, which distrusts national myths of unbroken continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from deference to natural science, which treats sex as biological; adherents may split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Identity politics is outside technocracy's concerns; inferred as neutral.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: sacralising sacrifice is a symbolic, emotive politics contrary to technocracy's rational, results-focused style.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Technocracy seeks reason and evidence rather than ideology; a spiritual good-versus-evil framing is its opposite (inferred from that rationalism).

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora and homeland questions are outside technocracy's core; inferred as neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: technocracy prioritises building competent institutions, not cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is outside technocracy's concerns; inferred as neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's secular, evidence-based criteria for judging institutions rather than moral-feminist tests.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: technocracy puts competence over group identity in who runs economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: territorial units are drawn for administrative efficiency, not ethnic unity.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a technocratic concern; technocrats are indifferent to union independence so long as expert administration is not obstructed (Veblen's soviet of technicians even assigns unions a role).

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Technocracy locates legitimacy in competence and results rather than worker power, and the 1930s Technocracy movement opposed partisan and revolutionary politics; inferred from that.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No stated position; technocrats judge ownership by efficiency and evidence, and hybrid technocratic states mix public and private provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred only; expert bodies are favoured but technocracy has no doctrine on legislative structure, and a unitary rational common good does not call for a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from Veblen's centrally coordinated industry run by engineers and the continental technate, which sit uneasily with ownership by individual municipalities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Caramani's account of a single common good worked out by experts, which favours binding decisions by expert bodies over purely local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats would set wages by economic evidence, not by a family-need principle.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Technocrats defer to regulatory expertise, but expert opinion is split between speed and caution, so adherents differ.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the faith in science and progress running from Saint-Simon onward; no specific doctrine on anti-ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the preference for data-driven, efficient administration, which favours traceable payments; not a stated position.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine is about expert rule, and technocrats differ between data-driven identification and privacy.

person-over-state.rationale: Technocracy pursues one rationally identified common good, which can sit against individual claims, but adherents do not state a view on treating persons as means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the materialist, abundance-and-efficiency orientation of technocracy, which treats politics as managing material provision.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the unitary, hierarchical conception of authority with central expert institutions; not stated directly.

gm-crops.rationale: Technocrats defer to scientific consensus, which finds approved genetically engineered crops safe, so they would embrace them as a sustainable tool.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the evidence-based planning orientation; expert urban and environmental planning generally favours compact cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anti-pluralism is defining: Caramani describes technocracy as rejecting the representation of competing group interests in favour of one common good.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy is indifferent to racial pride, though its claimed neutrality makes group identity politics foreign to it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Saint-Simon's view of war as a clash of private interests that enlightened rule would end; no direct position on defensive-only force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Technocracy is about competence in administration, not national identity; inferred from its universalist, evidence-based approach and from the transnational expert institutions it favours (EU bodies), which sit poorly with ethnolinguistic nationhood.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's pursuit of one common good worked out by reason, which treats group-based representation as entrenching partisan interests rather than expert judgment.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not an issue the sources discuss; inferred from technocrats' evidence-first stance, which discounts conspiracy-style claims lacking demonstrated evidence.

free-public-college.rationale: Technocrats value trained expertise and so broad access to education, but the sources say nothing on tuition and technocrats split between funding by the state and cost-sharing on efficiency grounds.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the efficiency orientation of technocratic policy, which tends to favour pricing externalities as cost-effective, though some technocrats prefer direct expert-set regulation.

future-generations.rationale: Technocracy stresses a single long-term common good over short electoral cycles, so long-horizon duties such as climate stewardship fit it; inferred rather than stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Technocracy grounds legitimacy in expertise rather than in the identity or typical values of groups; inferred from that principle, though not addressed in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from technocrats' preference for rational, negotiated and evidence-based security policy, while the qualifier on national safety leaves room for expert judgment.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Technocratic governance is often insulated from public scrutiny and relies on expert bodies negotiating confidentially, yet transparency of evidence is also valued; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

capital-controls.rationale: Technocrats are split: independent central banks and the IMF have mostly favoured open capital flows, while expert-run states such as Singapore and China manage them; the sources do not settle it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: technocrats favour effective state administration and rule-bound institutions, which fits a state monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: technocracy stresses orderly administration and expert command, which does not favour individual refusal of orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: Veblen's soviet of technicians and hybrid technocracies set conditions by expert administration, not by bargaining between interest groups.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: expert economists commonly favour targeted, evidence-based income supplements, though the sources do not discuss them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Technocratic governance hands key functions such as monetary policy and budget oversight to independent expert bodies bound by rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats differ on whether global rules should be redesigned for developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Technocracy works through professional administration and expert institutions, so it seeks to use and improve the existing state rather than smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: technocrats seek one common good worked out by reason, which leans against open-ended difference in systems, though they favour testing policies.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: technocrats favour measurement and accounting for resources, including natural-capital accounting, as part of evidence-based policy.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: technocracy rests on competence and results rather than on sacred or emotional loyalties.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: expert opinion tends to see across-the-board debt cancellation as poorly targeted, though the sources do not address it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the framing is a political-economy claim that technocracy's sources do not make, and technocrats treat regional gaps as problems for planning.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats split between respect for settled human dignity and enthusiasm for technological enhancement.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: technocrats value expert, evidence-based information and independent institutions, which fits public-service media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Technocracy is a doctrine about how to govern and takes no position on religious truth; it favours evidence over faith but does not rule on religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Technocrats would set farm policy by expert analysis, which could favour or oppose price guarantees; the sources give no position, so adherents are split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the expert-managed security and deterrence reasoning typical of technocratic governments; the sources do not address nuclear arms directly.

workers-own-party.rationale: Technocracy is anti-partisan and rejects class-based party politics in favour of a single common good, and the 1930s movement opposed partisan politics.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the evidence-based, health-driven approach of technocratic rule, which would treat the practice as a harm to be prohibited.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the meritocratic, rules-based outlook that rejects status-based legal distinctions.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the preference for expert, scientific classification (linguists' criteria) over political or local naming; the sources do not address it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Technocracy hands regulation to expert agencies that set rules in advance, rather than relying on lawsuits after the harm, as the reference literature describes for environmental and regulatory bodies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from legitimacy resting on expertise and competence, not on tradition or lineage; the sources do not discuss customary leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the evidence-led, long-term common-good orientation, with Wikipedia noting technocratic approaches to environmental problems; liberty is not a primary value for it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the preference for evidence on what works, which research generally finds weakens the case for fixed sentences, and for expert discretion over rigid rules.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats would decide by evidence on integration outcomes, which could support or only encourage language requirements.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not a defining issue; technocrats judge such rules by their measured economic effects, so there is no settled view.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; evidence on fraud and access is contested and technocrats would defer to the findings.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the secular, evidence-based basis of technocratic rule that does not favor any doctrine.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Technocracy grounds legitimacy in competence and results, so elections alone do not make a government good; Bertsou and Caramani describe this as set against will-based representation.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the deference to social-science evidence over traditional moral codes.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats would weigh the evidence of harm, and the hybrid model accepts expert emergency measures.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the efficiency-minded, evidence-based approach that economists commonly favor in consolidating benefits.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the merit-based principle that competence, not sex, qualifies a person for public service.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats defer to evidence and there is no settled view.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the deference to scientific consensus.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the preference for expert bodies to carry out policy goals.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: rule by expertise says nothing on how unowned land is first acquired.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's preference for impartial, rule-based expert institutions over political discretion.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Technocracy grounds legitimacy in scientific, evidence-based method, which sits against literal reading of scripture as the basis for public decisions.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: not a technocratic concern, but expert, evidence-minded governance generally backs inclusive, rights-based design.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the 1930s movement favoured central planning but the mainstream hybrid doctrine is economically agnostic, so adherents are split.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Veblen's soviet of technicians and the preference for experts selected through bodies rather than popular vote.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: privileging a national church is a identity-based claim, not an expert or evidence-based one.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: territorial autonomy is a question of political bargaining that technocracy does not address, and efficiency arguments cut both ways.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's scepticism of popular will as a basis for decisions, which Caramani contrasts with expert reason.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: border questions are not addressed; stability and efficiency arguments favour keeping borders but experts have no settled line.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from technocracy's faith in technology and efficiency to deliver abundance rather than limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the doctrine, so adherents are split.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is indifferent to conscription, which adherents would judge case by case on efficiency.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: technocracy rests on evidence and competence rather than appeals to ancestral or spiritual ties.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from its stress on evidence, procedure and rational administration, which is hard to square with killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats would judge by expert assessment of national interest, so no general answer follows.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy is indifferent to ethnic kinship and would treat it case by case.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream doctrine; the 1930s movement treated resources as a shared continental stock, but that strand is excluded.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; technocracy has no doctrine of rights and judges policy by outcomes.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the expert consensus that broad consumption taxes are an efficient revenue source.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from its efficiency and evidence-based approach, which favours measured, targeted programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Technocracy does bypass parties in favour of experts (non-pluralist, unitary representation), but not in favour of a leader, so this statement only half fits.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from Veblen's critique of business sabotage and its claim to neutral rules; stated only loosely.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its secular, reason-based claim to legitimacy.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Saint-Simon's attack on the maxim 'No innovation' and its faith in progress lean toward modernity over a return to tradition; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its evidence-based, rights-neutral expert approach, which generally follows modern legal consensus.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; technocrats judge by efficiency, and the question is a matter of national interest rather than expertise.

missingStatements.text: Politics should aim at one common good worked out by reason rather than balancing the competing interests of different groups.
missingStatements.rationale: Anti-pluralism, the pursuit of a single rationally identified general interest instead of mediating between groups, is a defining feature of technocracy in both the reference literature and the scholarship.

notes: Technocracy claims to be value-neutral, so on many social and moral statements it takes no position (0, low confidence); these zeros reflect indifference, not a split. The 1930s Technocracy Inc. strand would answer differently on economics: strongly against markets and money and for central planning (abolish-money-wages +2, central-planning +2, markets-allocate-better -2). Economic answers on the mainstream also split between Keynesian and neoliberal technocrats. The Caramani source was read as its published abstract only.
